items.title: Cancellation can overwrite a concurrently finalized heartbeat run
items.body:
### Pre-submission checklist

- [x] I have searched existing open and closed issues and this is not a duplicate.
- [x] I am on the latest released version of Paperclip (or can reproduce on `master`).
- [x] I have confirmed the error originates in Paperclip itself — not in my agent adapter, API provider, or local configuration.

### What happened?

A heartbeat cancellation can overwrite a terminal result that was committed concurrently

Both `cancelRun` and `cancelActiveForAgent` first observe a run while it is active, then later persist `cancelled` without requiring the run to still be in a cancellable state.

The race can occur as follows:

1. Cancellation observes a heartbeat run as `running`
2. A normal finalizer concurrently transitions the run from `running` to `succeeded` or `failed`
3. Cancellation resumes and writes `cancelled`
4. The already-terminal result and its metadata are replaced by cancellation state

`cancelActiveForAgent` has the same problem across its select-then-iterate path: a run can finalize after being included in the active-run snapshot but before the cancellation write reaches it

I reproduced both paths deterministically with promise barriers. No sleeps are required

### Expected behavior

The first successful terminal transition should remain authoritative

Once a heartbeat run has reached `succeeded` or `failed`, a cancellation that started from an earlier active-state snapshot should not replace that terminal result

Cancellation-specific persisted side effects should only run when the transition from a currently cancellable state to `cancelled` actually succeeds

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start from current `master`

2. Create a heartbeat run in `running` state with the normal associated wakeup state

3. Start `cancelRun(runId)` and pause the cancellation path after it has observed the run as cancellable but before the persisted cancellation status write

4. While cancellation is paused, finalize the same run using the normal conditional finalization transition:

   `running -> succeeded`

5. Resume cancellation

6. Read the heartbeat run again

7. Observe that the persisted status is `cancelled` rather than `succeeded`, and the terminal result metadata has been replaced by cancellation metadata

The same reproduction works with:

`running -> failed`

A second deterministic case reproduces the issue in `cancelActiveForAgent`:

1. Let the active-run query select a `running` run
2. Finalize that run before the cancellation loop writes its status
3. Resume the loop
4. Observe that the finalized run is still treated and counted as cancelled

I have regression tests using promise barriers for all three cases and can include them with the fix PR


### Paperclip version or commit

4d82f5eaea81690f0888eb7de8329ab2fd9849bf

### Deployment mode

Local dev (pnpm dev)

### Installation method

Built from source (pnpm dev / pnpm build)

### Agent adapter(s) involved

- [ ] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Cursor
- [ ] Droid
- [ ] Hermes
- [ ] Custom / external plugin adapter
- [x] Not adapter-specific (core bug)

### Database mode

None

### Access context

None

### Node.js version

v24.11.0

### Operating system

Debian 12 (bookworm) Docker container

### Relevant logs or output

```shell
Deterministic regression run against the unmodified baseline:

Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       3 failed | 111 skipped (114)

cancelRun vs successful finalization:

Expected:
  status: succeeded
  resultJson:
    terminalMarker: successful-finalizer-metadata

Received:
  status: cancelled
  resultJson:
    stopReason: cancelled

cancelRun vs failed finalization:

Expected:
  status: failed
  resultJson:
    terminalMarker: failed-finalizer-metadata
    failureDetail: recognizable failure

Received:
  status: cancelled
  resultJson:
    stopReason: cancelled

cancelActiveForAgent race:

Expected cancelled count: 0
Received cancelled count: 1
```

### Relevant config (if applicable)

```json

```

### Additional context

This appears to be an asymmetric terminal-transition guard

Normal heartbeat finalization already uses a conditional transition from `running`, so a late finalizer does not overwrite a cancellation that won first

The cancellation paths currently perform their active-state observation before the final cancellation write. The final write is not conditioned on the run still being in `queued`, `running`, or `scheduled_retry`

As a result:

- finalization cannot overwrite a completed cancellation
- cancellation can overwrite a completed finalization

The reproduced consequences are limited here to persisted lifecycle behavior:

- `succeeded` or `failed` can become `cancelled`
- terminal result/error metadata can be replaced
- the associated wakeup can be changed to cancelled
- cancellation-specific lifecycle/cleanup behavior can run after another terminal transition already won

Issue execution-lock cleanup uses run-aware predicates, so I am not claiming that successor issue ownership is necessarily corrupted by this race

The reproduction was run from source under Node.js 24.11.0 in a Debian bookworm Docker container using the repository's embedded PostgreSQL test environment

I have a narrow local fix and deterministic regression coverage and plan to open a PR after filing this issue

### Privacy checklist

- [x] I have reviewed all pasted output for PII (usernames, file paths, API keys, tokens, company names) and redacted where necessary.

items.title: No agent-writable field on the heartbeat run record
items.body:
# Upstream report A — no agent-writable field on the run record

**Type:** feature request / API gap
**Versions checked:** `@paperclipai/server` 2026.817.0 (installed and running here, confirmed via `GET /api/health` → `"serverVersion":"2026.817.0"`) and 2026.824.0 (npm dist-tag `latest`, tarball downloaded and read on 2026-08-25). The gap is present in both.

---

## Summary

An agent running inside a Paperclip heartbeat run cannot write anything to its own run row. There is no HTTP surface — none at all — that lets an authenticated agent token attach a structured annotation, a health signal, or a key/value pair to the `heartbeat_runs` record it is executing under. Everything an agent might want to surface on the board about its own run has to be redirected onto some other entity (an issue comment, a document, a work product), which breaks the association a board operator is actually looking at when they open a run.

The concrete need: when a lane detects that it lost grounding (a dependency was unreachable, a data source returned stale results, a verification step was skipped), that fact belongs on the run, because the run is what an operator inspects when they ask "was this heartbeat trustworthy?". Today it can only be recorded next to the run.

## What exists today

Run-scoped HTTP routes in `server/dist/routes/agents.js` (2026.817.0):

| Route | Method | Agent-writable? |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}` | GET | read only |
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/events` | GET | read only |
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/log` | GET | read only |
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/workspace-operations` | GET | read only |
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/issues` | GET | read only (`routes/activity.js:313`) |
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/cancel` | POST | no — handler opens with `assertBoard(req)` (`agents.js:3121`) |
| `/api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/watchdog-decisions` | POST | yes, but a fixed enum |

There is no `PATCH /api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}` and no `POST /api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/events`. The only run-scoped POST an agent token can actually reach is `/watchdog-decisions`, which accepts `snooze | continue | dismissed_false_positive` and drives stranding recovery (`recovery.recordWatchdogDecision`). Writing annotation data through it would suppress legitimate re-wakes, so it is not an annotation surface even informally.

## Why the adjacent surfaces do not close the gap

**`resultJson`.** The column exists (`packages/db/dist/schema/heartbeat_runs.js:21`, `jsonb("result_json")`) but is written only by the harness at finalization, from the adapter's return value. An agent has no way to merge a key into it mid-run.

**The `process` adapter.** It parses no stdout sentinel. `adapters/process/execute.js` returns `resultJson: { stdout: proc.stdout, stderr: proc.stderr }` verbatim on both the success and the non-zero-exit path (lines 66–86). There is no documented marker an agent could emit on stdout that the adapter would lift into a structured field.

**No spare column.** `heartbeat_runs` has `usage_json`, `result_json`, and `context_snapshot`, and no `metadata`. Verified in 2026.817.0 and again in 2026.824.0 — `packages/db/dist/schema/heartbeat_runs.js` is unchanged in this respect.

**The live status fields are not persisted state.** `currentStatusMessage`, `currentToolName`, and `lastAssistantSnippet` are decorated onto the response at read time by `heartbeat.decorateActiveRunStatus(run)` from an in-process registry. No HTTP route reaches that registry, so an agent cannot set them.

**`POST /api/companies/{companyId}/activity`** has exactly the right shape — a `runId` foreign key plus a `details` jsonb — but the handler opens with `assertBoard(req)` (`routes/activity.js:283`), so an agent token gets 403. (Its OpenAPI document nevertheless advertises `x-paperclip-authorization: {"actor":"board_or_agent"}` and `AgentBearerAuth`. That is a separate defect, reported separately.)

## Precedent already in the codebase

`POST /api/issues/{id}/work-products` does the thing we are asking for, one entity over: it accepts arbitrary `metadata`, exposes `healthStatus` as a real enum field, and the server stamps `createdByRunId` from the authenticated run rather than trusting a client-supplied id. That is exactly the ownership model a run-annotation surface would need — the same pattern, applied to the run itself.

## What would close this

Any one of these:

1. **A run-scoped annotations endpoint.** `POST /api/heartbeat-runs/{runId}/annotations`, agent-writable when the authenticated run *is* `{runId}`, writing to a new jsonb column (`annotations_json`) or an append-only `heartbeat_run_annotations` table. Server stamps the writer the way work-products stamps `createdByRunId`.
2. **Scoped `resultJson` merge.** Allow an agent token to merge keys into its own run's `resultJson` under a reserved namespace (e.g. `agent`), leaving the harness-owned keys untouched at finalization.
3. **A documented stdout sentinel.** Have the `process` adapter recognise a line-delimited marker (e.g. `::paperclip:run-annotation:: {json}`) and lift it into a first-class run field instead of leaving it buried in `stdoutExcerpt`.

Option 1 is the cleanest: it does not overload a field the harness owns, and it composes with the existing read routes.

## Impact if left as-is

Run-level quality signals become invisible at the level where they are read. An operator opening a run sees status, exit code, and a stdout excerpt — a lane that knowingly degraded looks identical to one that did not. Every workaround (comment, document, work product) moves the signal to an entity the operator has to know to go look at.

items.title: fix(heartbeat): claim task ownership with queued runs
items.body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip manages agents and their tasks.
> - The scheduler can start several runs for one agent.
> - Each task still needs one execution owner.
> - Task creation and recovery can queue assignments for the same task.
> - The scheduler previously marked both runs running before starting either executor.
> - This change claims the run and task ownership in one transaction.
> - Tasks with different IDs retain concurrent execution.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #13882. Related queue work: #11830 and #13965; those address different admission and cancellation paths.

**What happened?**

The Grok subscription Product campaign exposed two assignment runs for one task. Task creation and periodic recovery started runs within 200 ms. Both acquired Daytona sandboxes. One failed before provider work with `paperclip_runner_attachment_staging_not_authorized` because the other owned the task. Fixture cleanup then found an active session. The original failed result is retained in [campaign 36071063537](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/actions/runs/36071063537).

**Expected behavior**

Only the task execution owner may start provider setup. Competing queued work must wait. Different tasks may use the agent's available slots.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Set an agent's concurrent run limit to two.
2. Queue task-creation and recovery assignment runs for the same task.
3. Resume the queue while holding adapter execution open.
4. Before this fix, both runs become running. Only one has the task execution lock.

**Paperclip version or commit**

Reproduced on master `8781f06a8` and in the Grok campaign at `4196a4cd`.

## What Changed

- Use the same company-scoped task ownership gate for assignments, direct comments, and queued comments.
- Leave competing work queued while another live run owns the task. Transfer a terminal pointer only after the tracked executor and durable environment leases/finalization settle, including cleanup on another controller.
- Commit the running state and task execution owner together.
- Preserve the dedicated review path and the native replacement checkout guard.
- Add sixteen database regressions for assignment/comment orderings, unrelated concurrent tasks, and cross-controller cleanup fences.

## Verification

- Live subscription Product E2E planning passed on its first attempt in both Daytona (351,197 ms) and local execution (268,883 ms), with 6/6 matchers and cleanup passing in each, on combined source `1b0551bb7c8de3c54f4bee64dbe2c88328b3645e` ([campaign](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/actions/runs/36080870743)). The local screenshots and persisted state show the same plan revised, the first approval rejected, the revised approval accepted, and one completion. The full campaign remains unqualified because of a separate startup retry and EC2 Spot interruption.
- The new same-task regression failed before the fix: two running rows instead of one.
- All seven focused concurrency cases passed. Three comment cases failed before the shared gate was added. Five cross-controller cleanup cases failed before the durable gate was added. A warm-retention regression also failed before its successful release receipt was admitted; missing/failed receipts and a different retention policy stay blocked.
- `node ../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/__tests__/heartbeat-stale-queue-invalidation.test.ts` from `server`: 48 passed. Native cleanup admission adds one passing test; task-drain release adds two. Total focused checks: 51 passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/actions/runs/36078495577) passes repository typecheck, tests, Rust checks, build, and browser suites. The unrelated repository-form browser shard passed one bounded rerun without assertion or code changes; its original navigation failure remains retained. No local Docker or Rust build was used.
- The failed test's exact two sandboxes were checked: one was already absent; the other was deleted after its company, environment, and run labels matched.

## Risks

The claim transaction adds a task row lock. It follows task-before-run lock order. A competing run stays queued until the current owner releases the task. The change does not alter attachment authorization, provider permissions, schemas, or public APIs. Review is 5/5 with all threads resolved on `23c0d13b6`. All CI checks pass on that exact head. Live Grok requalification will use the combined runner and scheduler source.

## Model Used

OpenAI GPT-6 through Codex, with repository tools and code execution. The exact serving identifier and context-window size are not exposed in this session.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have specified the model used (with version and capability details)
- [x] I have checked ROADMAP.md and confirmed this PR does not duplicate planned core work
- [x] I have searched GitHub for duplicate or related PRs and linked them above
- [x] I have either (a) linked existing issues with `Fixes: #` / `Closes #` / `Refs #` OR (b) described the issue in-PR following the relevant issue template
- [x] I have not referenced internal/instance-local Paperclip issues or links (only public GitHub `#NNN` / `github.com/paperclipai/paperclip` URLs)
- [x] My branch name describes the change (e.g. `docs/...`, `fix/...`) and contains no internal Paperclip ticket id or instance-derived details
- [x] I have run tests locally and they pass
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation to reflect my changes
- [x] I have considered and documented any risks above
- [x] All Paperclip CI gates are green
- [x] Greptile is 5/5 with no open P2s, recommendations, or follow-ups
- [x] I will address all Greptile and reviewer comments before requesting merge

### Live regression verification

The Daytona plan/revise/accept lifecycle in [Grok campaign 36080870743](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/actions/runs/36080870743) passed on its first attempt at combined source `1b0551bb7c8de3c54f4bee64dbe2c88328b3645e`, in 351,197 ms, with all six outcome matchers and cleanup passing. The earlier competing-run failure remains retained. This is one live planning result; the complete Grok matrix and repeated qualification are separate gates, and this campaign also has separately retained infrastructure failures.
